title: Independence of coordinates of a random matrix–vector product
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A$ be a random $k\times d$ real matrix, that is, a measurable map assigning to each $\omega\in\Omega$ a matrix $A(\omega)\in\bbr^{k\times d}$. Suppose the rows of $A$ are mutually independent, meaning the $k$ random vectors $\omega\mapsto\bigl(A(\omega)_{i,1},\dots,A(\omega)_{i,d}\bigr)\in\bbr^{d}$, for $i=1,\dots,k$, are mutually independent under $\mu$. Then for every fixed $x\in\bbr^{d}$ the $k$ coordinates of the product $A(\omega)\,x$, namely the real-valued random variables $\omega\mapsto (A(\omega)\,x)_i=\sum_{j=1}^{d}A(\omega)_{i,j}\,x_j$ for $i=1,\dots,k$, are mutually independent under $\mu$.
hypotheses_covered: A is a random k×d real matrix
the rows of A are mutually independent random vectors
x is a fixed vector in ℝ^d
replaced:
If the row vectors of $A$ (as $(\mathrm{Fin}\,d\to\mathbb{R})$-valued random
variables) are mutually independent under $\mu$, then for any fixed
$x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ the scalar row-projections
$(A\,\omega).\texttt{toEuclideanLin}\,x\,i = \sum_j A_{\omega,i,j}\,x_j$
are independent across $i\in\mathrm{Fin}\,k$, since each is a measurable
function of a distinct row of $A$.
